Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 35-year-old male with new-onset episodic frontal headaches, palpitations, intermittent shortness of breath, bilateral hand tingling, heat intolerance, unintentional 5-lb weight loss, and loss of libido. Symptoms started after job change; occur predominantly at work. Past history of “hyperthyroidism” taking thyroxine.  
- Differential considerations:  
  • Possible iatrogenic hyperthyroidism (over-replacement) – supported by heat intolerance, weight loss, palpitations, and thyroxine use.  
  • Stress-related anxiety/panic episodes with tension-type headaches – temporal link to work stress; SOB and tingling could be hyperventilation.  
  • Primary tension or migraine headaches triggered by screen use – frontal pain with mild nausea.  
- No red-flag neurological features reported, but in-person exam required.  
- Plan (tele-visit): Arrange face-to-face appointment for full physical examination (heart, lungs, neurological). Order blood tests including thyroid function (TSH, free T4/T3) and routine panel. No medications started pending evaluation.  

Management Plan
-  In-person clinic appointment to be booked by patient via app.  
-  Physical examination (cardiac, respiratory, neurological).  
-  Blood tests: Thyroid function, plus baseline CBC, electrolytes (doctor indicated “blood tests for your thyroxine”).  
-  Reassess after results; consider endocrinology referral if thyroid dysfunction confirmed.  
-  Provide stress-management advice as appropriate after evaluation.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism from excess thyroxine – High likelihood; classic hyper-thyroid symptoms while on replacement therapy.  
2. Stress-related anxiety/panic disorder with tension-type headaches – Moderate likelihood; strong temporal association with work stress.  
3. Primary tension or migraine headaches – Moderate likelihood; screen-time trigger, mild nausea.
